integratedBehavior: The local project is a relocatable versioned directory package whose non-sensitive root manifest, protected state, objects, indexes, caches, models, configuration, exports, logs, locks, and temporary data have explicit authority, retention, backup, deletion, and portable-export classifications.

Create stages and verifies a complete package before atomic publication. Open uses stable Windows directory identities and an exclusive lock; close releases it; archive/restore are reversible manifest transitions; recoverable delete moves only the project package and requires exact identity confirmation, never deleting the shared model cache.

Audit publication rejects redirect, hardlink, multi-link, non-regular, changed-identity, oversized, and malformed targets. Audit or filesystem failure rolls back exact manifest, lock, internal-open, and root state or produces a bounded recovery error.

Current compatible projects open read-write. Structurally valid older, newer, or application-incompatible projects open only read-only with no package, lock, or audit mutation. Damaged/incomplete packages fail closed, and every incompatible state maps to one exact backup-first recovery action.

The production Projects workspace implements only functional CAP-02.S01 actions. It does not embed or expose the UI reference site, and incompatible projections expose no archive, restore, or delete mutation control.
failureAndRecoveryCoverage: invalid, relative, device-namespace, installation-root, redirected, hardlinked, oversized, malformed, incomplete, unsafe-field, unknown-format, and stable-root substitution paths
concurrent open, stale or mismatched lock, audit hardlink/identity/write failure, open/delete rollback, publish/rename failure, wrong delete confirmation, and shared-cache preservation

older migration-required, newer unsupported, application-incompatible, reversed/unsafe version ranges, swapped recovery actions, mismatched deletion identity, restart, and exact no-write read-only close/reopen
archived-incompatible mutation suppression, keyboard/focus return, offline zero-request behavior, theme/responsive/accessibility parity, and clear backup-first user guidance
performance baseline byte/source/value laundering, non-finite values, measurement-only false evidence, single-run scheduler variance, absolute budget, and relative regression denial
